result.title: Sparse Adaptation for In-Context Learning on Data Streams
result.summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data streams, making edge computing essential for low-latency applications and 5G networks. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable adaptation through in-context examples rather than parameter updates, but evolving streams challenge context relevance and computational efficiency. This work introduces SAIL, a framework for sparse adaptation of TFMs that reuses the model's key--value cache between adaptation events. SAIL reconstructs its support set only when drifts in stream structure indicate potential context inadequacy, while the structural representation itself is updated by changes in predictive performance. SAIL combines prequential error monitoring with online, class-specific micro-clustering to detect changes in cluster mass, class separability, and feature-space coverage. Upon adaptation, a context budget is allocated proportionally to class mass, and the most recently updated micro-clusters provide representative observations for refitting. This limits context redundancy and computational cost while preserving recent structural information.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SAIL，面向表格基础模型在数据流上的稀疏自适应：复用适配事件之间的 KV cache，仅在聚类质量、类可分性和特征空间覆盖显示漂移时才重建上下文支持集，并按类质量比例分配上下文预算，从而控制冗余与计算开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「漂移触发才重建上下文」与 KV cache 跨事件复用、按预算挑选代表性样本的做法，可能为 LVR 中缓存结构与视觉证据筛选、以及何时更新推理状态的决策提供借鉴线索；但任务为表格数据流，与多模态推理距离较远，需核查可迁移性。
